evidence: application-sign-in-policy.v1 closes the configuration to none, windows-password, and windows-hello, requires schemaVersion 1.0 and policyRevision, and permits zero inactivity minutes only with protected modes.

An absent canonical and predecessor state is atomically materialized as explicit none. Every accepted application-lock-profile.v1.json migrates to windows-password while preserving the exact profile name and every supported zero/nonzero timeout; invalid canonical state never falls back to legacy or none.
Preparation verifies the destination before none-to-protected changes and verifies the configured current provider followed by the destination before protected-provider switches.

The prepared transition binds the exact source authority and identities, source and target modes, target digest, proof class, warning duty, lock generation, and expiry. Commit rechecks those bindings under the cross-process arbiter before compare-and-swap publication.

Protected-to-none requires the configured provider before the warning/confirmation stage. Corrupt or unavailable-provider recovery is a separate explicit password-recovery path and accepts only the existing native LogonUserW plus EqualSid same-process-user proof.

Renderer possession, confirmation, audit data, or a transition handle cannot create proof. The opaque handle is represented natively only by a SHA-256 digest and is useful only with its exact native bindings and confirmation.

Cancelled, denied, unavailable, busy, failed, conflict, and expired outcomes are distinct and strictly decoded. Every verification failure and stale/concurrent attempt preserves the committed policy bytes.

Publication uses a cryptographically unique same-directory staging file, flush, atomic Windows replace/create with write-through, stable path and file identities, a named cross-process mutex, and compare-and-swap. A failed publication preserves retry authority and prior bytes; a response-lost retry returns the same committed receipt.
Explicit none is unlocked and manual, restart, and idle locking are no-ops. A protected zero-minute profile is manual-only; a protected nonzero profile locks on restart and inactivity.

Malformed, unreadable, corrupt, unknown-version, or authority-changed state is invalid/recovery-only and remains locked. Unavailable, denied, cancelled, stale, or mismatched recovery cannot mutate the policy.
